papers.title: Improving Uncertainty Sampling with Bell Curve Weight Function
papers.abstract: Typically, a supervised learning model is trained using passive learning by randomly selecting unlabelled instances to annotate. This approach is effective for learning a model, but can be costly in cases where acquiring labelled instances is expensive. For example, it can be time-consuming to manually identify spam mails (labelled instances) from thousands of emails (unlabelled instances) flooding an inbox during initial data collection. Generally, we answer the above scenario with uncertainty sampling, an active learning method that improves the efficiency of supervised learning by using fewer labelled instances than passive learning. Given an unlabelled data pool, uncertainty sampling queries the labels of instances where the predicted probabilities, p, fall into the uncertainty region, i.e., $p \approx 0.5$. The newly acquired labels are then added to the existing labelled data pool to learn a new model. Nonetheless, the performance of uncertainty sampling is susceptible to the area of unpredictable responses (AUR) and the nature of the dataset. It is difficult to determine whether to use passive learning or uncertainty sampling without prior knowledge of a new dataset. To address this issue, we propose bell curve sampling, which employs a bell curve weight function to acquire new labels. With the bell curve centred at p=0.5, bell curve sampling selects instances whose predicted values are in the uncertainty area most of the time without neglecting the rest. Simulation results show that, most of the time bell curve sampling outperforms uncertainty sampling and passive learning in datasets of different natures and with AUR.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种改进的主动学习采样方法，但未涉及有限元代理建模或生物力学设计，与用户研究方向关联度低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on active learning for general classification tasks, with no FEA surrogate modeling, no uncertainty quantification for physical simulations, and no biomedical or implant design context.

summary_en.motivation: To reduce labeling cost in active learning by improving sampling efficiency over standard uncertainty sampling.
summary_en.method: Proposes bell curve sampling, which uses a bell-shaped weight function centered at p=0.5 to select instances near the decision boundary while occasionally sampling others.
summary_en.result: Bell curve sampling outperforms both uncertainty sampling and passive learning across datasets of varying nature and uncertainty regions.
summary_en.validation: Validated through numerical simulations on multiple classification benchmark datasets.
